title: Virtues and Flaws Basics
heading: Chapter 4: Virtues and Flaws
summary: How Virtues and Flaws are bought and balanced: Virtues cost points, Flaws grant them, Minor and Major sizes, the cap on Flaws for a central character, and what makes a Flaw acceptable to the troupe.
quotes: Major Virtues cost three points, while Major Flaws grant three points.
A central character may have up to ten points of Flaws, but no more than five Minor Flaws.

title: Social Status Requirement
heading: Social Status Virtues and Flaws
summary: Every character must have a Social Status Virtue or Flaw to show how society sees them, usually limited to the society of the saga; some statuses are restricted by how society perceives the character's gender.
quotes: every character must have one of these, to represent the way that society sees them

title: Virtue and Flaw Limits
heading: Virtues and Flaws Rules and Guidelines
summary: General limits on taking Virtues and Flaws: repeats only when allowed, one Social Status, and guidelines for Story and Personality Flaws.
quotes: A Virtue or Flaw may be taken more than once only if the description explicitly allows it.
A character may not have more than one Major Personality Flaw.

title: Virtues and Flaws for Grogs
heading: Grogs
summary: Character-creation limits on Virtues and Flaws for grogs, including bans on Major Virtues and Flaws, Hermetic Virtues and The Gift.
quotes: You may take up to 3 points of Flaws, and an equal number of points of Virtues
You may not take Major Virtues or Flaws

title: Virtues and Flaws for Companions
heading: Companions
summary: Character-creation limits on Virtues and Flaws for companions, including Minor Flaw limits and Social Status requirement.
quotes: You may take up to 10 points of Flaws, and an equal number of points of Virtues
You may not have more than 5 Minor Flaws

title: Virtues and Flaws for Mythic Companions
heading: Mythic Companions
summary: Character-creation limits for Mythic Companions, who get extra Virtue points per Flaw point, a defining Free Virtue and a free Minor Virtue.
quotes: You make take up to 10 points of Flaws, and 2 points of Virtues for every 1 point of Flaws, for a maximum of 20 points of Virtues

title: Virtues and Flaws for Magi
heading: Magi
summary: Character-creation limits for magi: balanced Virtues and Flaws, at most one Major Hermetic Virtue, required Gift and Hermetic Magus status, and a free House Minor Virtue.
quotes: You must take The Gift and the Hermetic Magus Social Status Virtue
You may not have more than one Major Hermetic Virtue

title: The Gift (Virtue Type)
heading: The Gift
summary: Describes The Gift as a cost-free Virtue with its penalties, how it lets a character learn Supernatural Abilities and Hermetic Magic, and who should be allowed to have it.
quotes: The Gift is a special Virtue, because it has no cost.

title: Hermetic Virtues and Flaws
heading: Hermetic
summary: Only characters with The Gift can take Hermetic Virtues and Flaws; a troupe may let a character with many Supernatural Virtues take Hermetic Flaws as Supernatural Flaws.
quotes: Only characters with The Gift can take these Virtues and Flaws

title: Social Status Types
heading: Social Status
summary: Social Status Virtues and Flaws set a character's place in society, and some are Free and cost no points.
quotes: Some Social Status Virtues are Free, which means that they do not cost any points to buy.

title: Social Statuses by Culture
heading: Social Statuses by Culture
summary: Explains that available Social Statuses depend on culture and lists, per culture, which Free, Minor and Major Virtues and Flaws are available.
quotes: Free Virtues
Hermetic Magus

title: Supernatural Virtues and Flaws
heading: Supernatural
summary: Supernatural Virtues and Flaws are tied to one of the four realms, which governs interaction with auras and grants immunity to Warping from a high aura of the same realm.
quotes: a character with a Supernatural Virtue or Flaw is immune to Warping caused by living in a high aura associated with the same realm

title: Personality Flaws
heading: Personality
summary: Guidance on Major and Minor Personality Flaws, including how they drive stories, how often they may be ignored, and limits on how many a character takes.
quotes: A character may not have more than one Major Personality Flaw
Most characters should not have more than two Personality Flaws, Major or Minor

title: Story Flaws
heading: Story
summary: Story Flaws are external hooks that drag a character into stories; limited to one per character and must depend on something outside the character.
quotes: You should not take more than one Story Flaw, Major or Minor

title: Personality and Story Flaw Frequency
heading: Personality & Story Flaws
summary: Advice for storyguides on limiting Major Personality and Story Flaws so that each has a chance to appear in play.

title: Tainted Virtues and Flaws
heading: Tainted Virtues and Flaws
summary: Tainted Virtues and Flaws are Infernal; sets limits on how many a character can take at creation and notes that granted supernatural abilities are Infernal powers.
quotes: no more than half a character's Virtues should be tainted
Supernatural abilities granted by Tainted Virtues or Flaws are always Infernal powers.
related: Realms of Power: The Infernal, chapter 9

title: Abilities Overview and Ability Rolls
heading: Chapter 5: Abilities
summary: Introduces Abilities and the basic Ability roll: add a Characteristic and an Ability to a die roll and meet or exceed an Ease Factor, with the Characteristic chosen to fit the situation.
quotes: Abilities are normally used by adding Characteristic + Ability + die roll, and meeting or exceeding an Ease Factor.

title: Specializations
heading: Specializations
summary: Each Ability except Spell Mastery gets a specialization that raises the effective score when the specialization applies.
quotes: you act as if your score were one level higher than it actually is

title: Abilities With No Score
heading: Abilities With No Score
summary: Explains whether and how a character with no score in an Ability can use it, depending on whether the Ability is asterisked and whether any experience has been put in it.
quotes: she may use it as if it had a score of zero, but rolling three extra botch dice
Characters cannot use Supernatural Abilities unless they have at least one experience point in the Ability.

title: Ability Roll (summary box)
heading: Ability Roll:
summary: Summary box giving the standard Ability roll, the use of unscored Abilities and the specialization bonus.
quotes: Characteristic + Ability + die roll, meet or exceed the Ease Factor to succeed

title: Ability Types
heading: Ability Types
summary: Lists the six types of Ability and notes that they are used alike, the difference being who may learn them.
quotes: There are six types of Ability

title: General Abilities (type)
heading: General Abilities
summary: General Abilities can be learned by almost anyone with no game restrictions.
quotes: there are no game restrictions on who may do so

title: Academic Abilities (type)
heading: Academic Abilities
summary: Academic Abilities need formal training, a Virtue or magus status for beginning characters, and usually a minimum score in a learned language.
quotes: Academic Abilities require formal training.
learning an Academic Knowledge normally requires a Latin, Greek, Hebrew, or Arabic score of at least 3

title: Arcane Abilities (type)
heading: Arcane Abilities
requires: Virtue granting the Ability, or magus
summary: Arcane Abilities may be bought at character generation only with a permitting Virtue or as a magus, and some Virtues also allow Penetration.
quotes: A character may only take these Abilities during character generation if permitted to by a Virtue, or if he is a magus.

title: Martial Abilities (type)
heading: Martial Abilities
requires: Virtue or Flaw granting the Ability, or magus
summary: Martial Abilities may be bought at character generation only with a permitting Virtue or Flaw, or as a magus.
quotes: Characters may only gain Martial Abilities during character generation if they are permitted to do so by a particular Virtue or Flaw, or if they are magi.

title: Spell Mastery Abilities (type)
heading: Spell Mastery Abilities
summary: Spell Mastery Abilities belong to magi and concern casting Formulaic and Ritual spells; full rules are in the Hermetic Magic chapter.
quotes: Spell Mastery Abilities can only be taken by magi

title: Supernatural Abilities (type)
heading: Supernatural Abilities
requires: Virtue granting the Ability, or The Gift
summary: Rules for obtaining Supernatural Abilities at creation, their realm of origin and the Warping immunity that goes with it, and how The Gift lets Gifted characters learn them in play.
quotes: Characters may only gain Supernatural Abilities during character creation if they have the Virtue granting the Ability.
If you have no reason to choose otherwise, your Ability is granted by the Magic realm

title: Animal Ken
heading: Animal Ken\*
summary: Lets the character communicate with animals, using their score as if it were skill in a language the animal speaks fluently.
quotes: Treat your score in Animal Ken as your score in a language that the animal speaks fluently in order to determine how well you can communicate

title: Art of Memory
heading: Art of Memory\*
summary: Memory-palace technique: the number of loci depends on the score, and a Complex Memorization roll against an Ease Factor lets the scholar remember a scene or writing in exact detail; those without the Ability can try with extra botch dice.
quotes: The character has a number of loci equal to five times their score in Art of Memory.
Stress Die + Intelligence + Art of Memory vs. Ease Factor of 9 (or higher)

title: Memorization Ease Factors
heading: Memorization Ease Factors
summary: Table of Ease Factors for memorizing letters, conversations, rooms and buildings, with adjustments for length, technical material and substitute Abilities.
quotes: 9 (Average)
If the subject matter is highly technical add 3 or even 6 to the Ease Factor.

title: Artes Liberales and Literacy
heading: Artes Liberales\*
summary: Artes Liberales is the foundation of academic study and also determines how many writing systems a character can read and write.
quotes: For every point in the Ability, the character can read and write one writing system

title: Brawl and Dodging
heading: Brawl
summary: Brawl covers unarmed and improvised-weapon fighting and is the Ability used to dodge when a character has no Martial Abilities.
quotes: Brawl is also the Ability used to dodge attacks if you have no Martial Abilities.

title: Chirurgy
heading: Chirurgy (kie-RUHR-gee)\*
summary: Medieval surgery used to help others recover from physical damage; the rules for its use are on the wound recovery page.
quotes: See page 405 for rules.

title: Concentration
heading: Concentration
summary: The storyguide may call for a Concentration roll before a demanding task or a retry after failure, and it helps magi hold spells through distractions.
quotes: the storyguide can call for a Concentration roll before you can make the attempt

title: Corpse Magic
heading: Corpse Magic\*
summary: Supernatural Ability to temporarily animate or question a suitable corpse, using a Casting Total and a Commanding roll compared against Ease Factors.
quotes: Communication + Corpse Magic + Aura modifier + stress die
Communication + Leadership + stress die

title: Corpse Magic Ease Factor Outcome
heading: Corpse Magic Ease Factor Outcome
summary: Table of what Corpse Magic achieves at each Ease Factor, including speaking to, animating and commanding corpses and the Ease Factors for commands.
quotes: Single word commands have an Ease Factor of 6, simple questions or commands require a 9, and more complex instructions or questions need a 12 or more.

title: Crafter's Healing
heading: Crafter's Healing\*
summary: Supernatural healing of wounds one level at a time at the cost of a Long-Term Fatigue level, using a roll against the Wound Recovery improvement Ease Factor, with Warping for the recipient.
quotes: Make a Presence + Crafter's Healing + stress die roll against an Ease Factor equal to the Improvement Ease Factor determined by the Wound Recovery Table

title: Curse-Throwing
heading: Curse-Throwing\*
summary: Supernatural Ability that moves diseases, curses and harmful effects from a sufferer to another recipient through a ritual, with a Casting Total against Ease Factors for the curse and modifiers for the recipient's link.
quotes: Presence + Curse-Throwing + Aura + stress die
PENETRATION TOTAL: Casting Total – Ease Factor + Penetration Bonus

title: Dowsing
heading: Dowsing\*
summary: Supernatural Ability to locate nearby things with a dowsing rod, with search time depending on area and Ease Factor depending on rarity and distance.
quotes: To find something common, like water, within 25 paces requires a Perception + Dowsing of 9+.

title: Enchanting (Ability)
heading: Enchanting (Ability)\*
summary: Supernatural performance Ability that sways emotions; roll Communication plus the Ability against Ease Factors for different effects, with Magic Resistance and botch rules.
quotes: An Ease Factor of 9 will calm the upset, 12 will win someone's love, 15 will incite a riot, and a 24 might win back a soul from the Prince of Darkness.

title: Entrancement
heading: Entrancement\*
summary: Supernatural Ability to command a person by eye contact, resolved against the target's Stamina roll with a bonus to the victim depending on how objectionable the command is.
quotes: Roll Presence + Entrancement against the target's Stamina roll.

title: Finesse
heading: Finesse
summary: Arcane Ability for manipulating spells and performing special feats with them, such as positioning objects delicately or targeting spells.
quotes: You would use this Ability to position objects delicately or to target spells.

title: Folk Ken
heading: Folk Ken
summary: Folk Ken lets a character read another person's background and motives, with the storyguide often rolling in secret so the player does not know the result.
quotes: Often the storyguide secretly rolls a die when this Ability is used.

title: Font of Knowledge
heading: Font of Knowledge\*
summary: Supernatural Ability letting a creature try a task using an untrained Ability, with an Ease Factor that rises with the number of uses in a day.
quotes: Intelligence + Font of Knowledge + stress die

title: Guile
heading: Guile
summary: Guile covers lying, feigning and disguise, often as an opposed roll; understanding the target gives a bonus.
quotes: roll 9+ on Perception + Folk Ken
It is often an opposed roll, against the victim's Perception + Folk Ken or, for disguise, Perception + Awareness.

title: Hex
heading: Hex\*
summary: Supernatural Ability to bring ruin on enemies by eye contact, occult signs or an Arcane Connection, with the chosen delay affecting potency.
quotes: There are three ways for her to activate this power

title: Hex Delay Modifiers and Roll
heading: Hex Delay Modifiers
summary: Delay modifiers table and Hex roll, including botch consequences, how hexes are removed, and treating a hex as a spell level when dispelling it.
quotes: Stress Die + Intelligence + Hex + Aura Bonus + Modifiers
Treat the hex as having a spell level equal to the number of botch dice it approximates, multiplied by 10

title: Hex Effects
heading: Hex Effects
summary: Chart of Hex Ease Factors by severity, each comparable to a number of botch dice, with example effects.
quotes: Minor (1 botch)
Terminal (5 botches)

title: Induction
heading: Induction\*
summary: Supernatural Ability to create illusions only the target perceives; Ease Factors rise with the risk the victim takes by believing the illusion, with roll modifiers, repeat attempts and rules for whether the victim realizes magic was used.
quotes: Attempts at induction require a die roll of Communication + Induction.
A victim of induction realizes afterwards that they have been affected by magic if the roll above does not exceed the Ease Factor by (6-1 per factor from the list below).

title: Entrancement and Induction
heading: Entrancement and Induction
summary: Explains how Entrancement and Induction differ and how a character with both can use each to support the other.
quotes: Entrancement takes control of a character's will, and dictates their actions, but does not affect what they believe or experience.

title: Legerdemain
heading: Legerdemain\*
summary: Sleight-of-hand Ability whose use is detected by the target rolling Perception plus Awareness, with a bonus to spot particularly delicate moves.
quotes: The target of an attempt rolls Perception + Awareness to detect your actions.

title: Living Languages
heading: (Living Language)\*
summary: Language Abilities measure how well a character communicates, with the lower score of two speakers setting the quality of conversation, penalties for related languages or dialects, and a table of fluency levels.
quotes: When two people speak to each other, the lower Ability score determines how well they communicate.

title: Magic Sensitivity
heading: Magic Sensitivity\*
summary: Supernatural Ability to sense the magical nature of places, items, spells and creatures, which lowers Magic Resistance and uses a roll against storyguide-set Ease Factors with guidelines for each target.
quotes: simply roll a simple die + Perception + Magic Sensitivity
Detecting a Magic aura would normally have an Ease Factor equal to 12 – aura level

title: Magic Theory
heading: Magic Theory\*
summary: Arcane Ability for the technical knowledge of Hermetic magic, used chiefly in the laboratory and of little use without The Gift.
quotes: Knowledge of what magic is and how it works, used primarily in the laboratory.

title: (Mystery Cult) Lore
heading: (Mystery Cult) Lore\*
requires: Membership or study of a Mystery Cult
summary: Cult-specific lore Ability covering rites, symbolism and signs of membership, needed for Initiation rites and some cult books; explains how experience is gained and what happens when it is learned without instruction.
quotes: In game terms, Experience points in Cult Lore are acquired like any other knowledge
A magus may build the knowledge from 0, even without instruction

title: Parma Magica
heading: Parma Magica\*
summary: Hermetic protection ritual that adds to Magic Resistance for a time, can be suppressed, can be extended to other people, and shields from the social penalties of other people's Gifts.
quotes: It lets you add 5 times your Parma Magica score to your Magic Resistance until the next sunrise or sunset, whichever comes first.
While a magus is protecting others, his effective Parma Magica score is reduced by 3 points

title: Persona
heading: Persona\*
summary: Supernatural Ability to assume different identities, changing appearance fully while keeping Characteristics, with one identity per point and a roll to change.
quotes: a roll of Stamina + Persona against an Ease Factor of 9
The character gains one identity for every point he has in the Persona Ability.

title: Premonitions
heading: Premonitions\*
summary: Supernatural Ability to sense approaching danger, rolled against an Ease Factor that depends on how imminent and serious the danger is.
quotes: Roll Perception + Premonitions against an Ease Factor depending on the situation.

title: Second Sight
heading: Second Sight\*
summary: Supernatural Ability to see through illusory concealment and naturally invisible things, with Ease Factors based on the magnitude of the concealing effect or fixed for invisible things.
quotes: All Second Sight rolls are Perception + Second Sight, and they are almost always simple rolls.
The Ease Factor to see through illusionary concealment is normally equal to 6 + the magnitude of the might of the creature responsible for the effect, or 6 + the magnitude of a Hermetic spell.

title: Sense Holiness and Unholiness
heading: Sense Holiness and Unholiness\*
summary: Divine Supernatural Ability to feel good and evil, with different Ease Factors for an area, a person or object, a demon and a hidden angel.
quotes: A Perception + Sense Holiness and Unholiness roll against an Ease Factor of 9 lets you sense holiness or unholiness in a general area; against an Ease Factor of 15, in a person or object.

title: Sense Passions
heading: Sense Passions\*
summary: Supernatural Ability to sense emotions and Personality Traits in beings and the tarnish or temper of auras, with a limited ability to recognize spirits and holy or unholy presences.
quotes: Stress Die + Perception + Sense Passions + Aura
related: Realms of Power: The Infernal, page 13
Realms of Power: The Divine Revised Edition, page 38

title: Shapeshifter
heading: Shapeshifter\*
summary: Supernatural Ability to take the shape of a mundane animal within a size range, with a Stamina roll to change and one shape known per point.
quotes: a roll of Stamina + Shapeshifter against an Ease Factor of 9
You have a limited repertoire of shapes, one for every point you have in the Shapeshift ability.

title: Stealth
heading: Stealth
summary: Stealth covers sneaking, hiding and following people unnoticed, the latter rolled against the other person's Perception.
quotes: which is rolled against the other person's Perception

title: Wilderness Sense
heading: Wilderness Sense\*
summary: Supernatural Ability to determine direction, weather, hazards or resources in the wild with one piece of information per roll.
quotes: A Perception + Wilderness Sense roll against an Ease Factor of 9 lets you determine the direction of north, the upcoming weather, or the presence of natural hazards or resources.
